title: Self-referencing foreign keys
description: A foreign key can reference its own table, modeling a hierarchy - here, `employees.manager_id` points at another row in `employees` itself. Write a query that returns the `first_name` and `manager_id` of every employee who has a manager.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: self-referencing FOREIGN KEY

manager_id REFERENCES employees (id) - the same table it lives in - so an employee row can point at another employee row to represent "reports to." A NULL manager_id means that person has no manager (they're at the top).
Select first_name and manager_id from employees, filtering to rows where manager_id IS NOT NULL.
expected_behavior: Returns first_name and manager_id only for employees that have a manager, in any order.
solution: SELECT first_name, manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL;
explanation: Self-referencing foreign keys are how SQL represents tree/hierarchy data with a plain table - no special syntax needed, just a column that references its own table's primary key.
